title: Window and Door Rebates in Kelowna 2026: $100 Each from FortisBC
desc: Kelowna's electricity comes from FortisBC, so FortisBC pays the $100 per window or door rebate, up to $2,000. 19,735 households live in pre-1981 homes. Rules and steps.
h1: Window and Door Rebates in Kelowna
lead: Kelowna's electricity comes from FortisBC, not BC Hydro, so the window and door rebate comes from FortisBC. It pays $100 for each window or door you replace, up to $2,000.
cards_heading: What FortisBC pays for windows and doors in Kelowna
cards_intro: We read FortisBC's window and door rebate listing on October 2, 2026 and checked it against BC Hydro's page, which uses the same amount. FortisBC lists the rebate for its gas and electric customers, and it is not available in the City of Vancouver.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: Paid by FortisBC for each window or door that replaces an existing one. Up to $2,000 in total.

cards.title: Energy rating
cards.note: We could not read the rating rules on FortisBC's tabbed page. Confirm the U-factor and certification there before you buy. BC Hydro's matching rebate needs U-1.22 W/m2-K or lower.

cards.title: Heating test
cards.note: Your primary heating system must be able to heat at least 50% of the home through the heating season.

cards.title: Second-upgrade bonus
cards.note: FortisBC adds $300 for a second upgrade, or an EnerGuide improvement bonus of $750 to $2,000.

cards.title: Lower incomes
cards.note: Income-qualified FortisBC customers can get free evaluations and upgrades.

after_cards:
A Kelowna 1970s house

A house with 12 windows, a front door and a sliding patio door is 14 openings. At $100 each that pays $1,400. Past 20 openings the $2,000 cap stops the rebate growing.
sections: The 2021 Census counted 62,210 households in Kelowna. About 19,735 (32%) live in homes built before 1981, and 8,205 are owner-occupied detached houses from that period. About 33% live in apartments and 35% rent. Only 3.9% say their home needs major repairs.

Kelowna's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was -3.2°C and the coldest day reached -24.0°C. Summers are hot. Replacement windows with a low U-factor slow heat flow through the glass in both seasons, which can help if the home is air conditioned.
Why FortisBC and not BC Hydro

BC Hydro's rebate is for BC Hydro accounts. In Kelowna, FortisBC supplies electricity, and it also runs the natural gas network. Either way, the FortisBC listing is the one to use. It asks that your primary heating system can heat at least half your home through the season to 22°C.

FortisBC pays per window or door replaced. In BC Hydro's version, each rough opening counts as one and a bay window counts as one, and skylights are excluded. Ask FortisBC to confirm the same counting on its listing before you sign a quote.

The rebate needs a U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower, and lower means less heat loss. Many window labels show the older imperial scale instead. To convert, multiply the imperial number by 5.678. A label that says U-0.30 equals 1.70 W/m2-K, which is too high. A label that says U-0.21 equals about 1.19 W/m2-K and passes. Ask the contractor to quote the metric value for each model so you do not have to convert.

BC Hydro publishes a consumer guide for window and door replacement. It covers frame materials, glazing types and what to ask a contractor. Read it before you take quotes, so you can compare units on the same terms. The program only checks the U-factor, certification and installation rules, so the other choices are yours.
FortisBC runs a free home evaluation and upgrade program for income-qualified customers, which can include insulation or heat pump upgrades. Ask about it before paying for any work.
claim_steps: Confirm your power bill says FortisBC.
Get quotes that list the U-factor of each unit.
Photograph the label on each unit.
Keep the invoice and apply to FortisBC online.
If your income may qualify, ask about the free program first.
faq: Do I apply to BC Hydro in Kelowna?
No. FortisBC supplies Kelowna's electricity, so apply to FortisBC.
$100 per window or door, up to $2,000.
FortisBC lists $300, or an EnerGuide improvement bonus of $750 to $2,000.
Does the City of Vancouver exclusion matter in Kelowna?
No. It applies only to homes in the City of Vancouver.
The average January low was -3.2°C and the coldest day in 2015 to 2024 was -24.0°C.
